title: The Stinson Method
logline: Robin trusts Lily with a nine-day secret, and Lily, who has never kept one, goes to Barney for lessons in lying. She graduates as a monster who beats a polygraph examiner and lies about everything, which unnerves Ted and Robin and scares Marshall half to death, and the one person most desperate for her to crack turns out to be Robin.
coldOpen: Kids, your Aunt Lily has never kept a secret in her life. Except for nine days in 2013, when she became the best liar in New York, and it terrified everyone who loved her.

couch.line: She told me who the killer was while we were still buying the tickets.
It was a cartoon about a penguin, Luke. She was right, though.

guests.name: Walt Krupnik
guests.role: a retired polygraph examiner, twenty-eight years with the New Jersey State Police, who never needed the machine: he reads lies off people's ears, announces 'True' or 'Lie' in a flat monotone after anything anyone says, and has never once been fooled

scenes.summary: Lily catches Robin buying shelf liner and a welcome mat. Robin whispers the secret: she bought an apartment, thirty-year mortgage, closing in nine days. Nobody can know, especially Marshall, and if it leaks Robin will never tell Lily anything again. Lily swears she's changed; flashback proves otherwise. Robin leaves, Marshall and Ted arrive, Lily starts singing, her tell. She bolts. Marshall is terrified and proud: forty seconds is her personal best.

beats.line: It started on a Tuesday, at the corner store, with the most suspicious shopping basket in New York.
Robin. Why are you buying shelf liner?
To line shelves. Like a normal adult.
You don't own shelves. You keep your scotch in the oven.
And a welcome mat? Robin, you have never welcomed anyone.
Okay. If I tell you, it never leaves this aisle.
Vault.
I bought an apartment. Thirty-year mortgage. I close in nine days.
Oh my god, you're stay—
Inside voice.
Thirty years? Robin, you dumped a guy for buying you a toothbrush.
It was electric. He was clearly planning a future.
Nobody knows until I close. Not Ted. Not Barney. Especially not Marshall.
Why especially Marshall?
He'll cry, then he'll knit me a doormat, then he'll cry about the doormat.
If this gets out, I'll know it was you. And I will never tell you anything again.
Robin, I'm the worst person in New York you could have told.
I know.
But I've changed. Last month Ted told me something huge, and I took it to my grave.
Lily, you can't tell anyone. I'm thinking about getting bangs.
Vault.
Marshall! Ted's getting bangs!
Ted, no! Not again!
I said thinking!
Your grave was sitting at the bar.
Nine days, Lily. Not a word.
Lilypad! We're getting nacho supplies. Was that Robin?
Doo doo doo, just a normal Tuesday, nobody bought anything.
She's singing.
She only sings when she has a secret.
Last Christmas you sang for six minutes, then told me my present. While I was unwrapping it.
Is it about me? Blink twice if it's about me.
La la la, blinking a normal amount.
Gotta go, love you, nothing's wrong, bye!
Ted. My wife has a secret. And she didn't tell me.
Marshall, it's been forty seconds.
That's her personal best! I'm terrified, and I'm so proud of her!

scenes.summary: Lily asks Barney to teach her to lie. He's thrilled to finally have an apprentice, on one condition: a final exam, and if he cracks her she tells him the secret. The Stinson Method, a snail-based alibi drill, and a four-day montage that kills her singing. Final exam: Walt Krupnik, a retired polygraph examiner who reads ears. Lily beats him by forgetting her husband exists, then tells Barney his Stormtrooper is a replica on her way out. Walt no longer knows anything.

beats.line: That night, Lily went to see the most dishonest man she knew. He was thrilled.
Let me get this straight. Lily Aldrin wants me to teach her to lie.
You lie for a living.
I don't lie for a living, Lily. I lie for fun. Nobody knows what I do for a living.
I have to keep one secret for nine days. Nine days, Barney.
What's the secret?
I can't tell you.
Wrong! Never say I can't tell you. It's a neon sign that says, ask me again.
What's the secret?
There's no secret, la la la.
And no innocent person has ever sung.
Why are you even helping me?
I've always wanted an apprentice. Ted can't lie, Marshall cries during, and Robin just shoots whoever's asking.
One condition. Final exam. If I crack you, you tell me the secret.
And if you can't?
Then I've built the greatest liar in New York. Second greatest.
Five rules. Memorize them, then deny you've ever seen them.
beats.title: The Stinson Method
lines: Add one boring detail. Nobody checks a boring detail.
Answer every question with a question.
Believe it. Then it's not a lie. It's a lifestyle.

beats.line: Drill. Where were you this afternoon?
At the store with Robin, she was buying shelf—
Rule two!
I was at the dentist. Dr. Pell. He has a new fish tank. It's mostly snails.
Beautiful. Nobody in history has ever fact-checked a snail.

beats.label: Four days of the Stinson Method

beats.line: I did not eat your yogurt.
Marine biologist. Mostly paperwork. Allergic to fish.
Did you sleep well?
Did you?
Barney, you have spinach in your teeth.
I haven't eaten spinach since 1994.
Final exam. Lily, meet my secret weapon.
Walt Krupnik. Twenty-eight years as a polygraph examiner with the New Jersey State Police. Never fooled once.
Don't need the machine. I watch the ears. The mouth lies. The ears confess.
Walt. Pleasure to have you.
Your left ear just went pink.
It's a genuine pleasure.
Pinker.
Lily. Where were you last Tuesday afternoon?
The dentist. Dr. Pell. New fish tank. Mostly snails.
True.
Did anyone tell you a secret this week?
Who would tell me a secret? Have you met me?
True.
Lily. Do you love Marshall?
Who's Marshall?
True.
I need to sit down. I once caught a man lying in his sleep.
Lily, you did it! You're a monster!
Thank you, Barney. You're the best teacher I've ever had.
Really?
Lie.
Oh, and Barney? Your Stormtrooper's a replica. The real one's been at Ted's since Christmas.
Walt. Was that a lie?
Son, I don't know anymore.

scenes.summary: Five days later. Marshall hasn't heard the toaster song all week, and her day was 'fine'. Robin pushes suspiciously hard for an interrogation; Ted is sure someone has a crush on him. Ted's taxi interrogation: good architect, bad architect. Lily deflects everything with snails and questions, turns Robin's real-estate hint back on her, tells Marshall she's never liked Bigfoot, and gets out of the cab after telling Ted one of his three admirers is in it. Marshall can't tell which loss he's crying about.

beats.line: Five days later, your Uncle Marshall hadn't slept, and I had a plan.
Five days, Ted. Not one song. Not in the shower. Not even the toaster song.
There's a toaster song?
Toast, toast, here comes the toast.
Every morning for nine years. Yesterday the toast came up, and she just took it.
I asked how her day was. She said fine. Lily doesn't have fine days. She has days with a villain and a twist.
So lean on her. Hard. Whatever she's holding, shake it loose.
Why do you care so much?
I'm a journalist, Ted. An unbroken story is like a loaded gun nobody's firing. It's a waste.
Relax. I already know what it is. Somebody has a crush on me.
Ted, not everything is about you.
Statistically, Robin, it's about me sixty percent of the time. I've charted it.
Here's the plan. She gets in, the doors lock, and nobody leaves this cab until she talks.
Good cop, bad cop?
Good architect, bad architect. I'm both. Bad architect mostly sighs.
Hi, guys.
Hi, Lilypad. How was your day?
Fine.
Fine, Ted!
Lily. Where were you on Tuesday the twelfth, at four p.m.?
The dentist. Dr. Pell. New fish tank. Mostly snails.
Lily, your dentist is Dr. Gupta.
Is she?
Sigh.
Lily. Has anyone you know made any big purchases lately? Hypothetically. In real estate.
Real estate?
Is that a question, Robin? Or a confession?
I hate this version of you.
Lilypad. I'm asking as your husband. Is there anything you're not telling me?
Marshall, I've never liked Bigfoot.
You made him a birthday card!
Did I?
Oh, and Ted? Three women have a crush on you. One of them is in this cab.
Robin?
Ted. She is lying about everything.
That's exactly what someone with a crush would say.
Bigfoot, Ted. My wife. Bigfoot.
I don't even know which one I'm crying about.

scenes.summary: Barney confesses to the gang that he trained Lily, and that he can't undo it: she's lying to people who already know her. He brings back Walt for one last test. Marshall's plea nearly breaks Lily, but she's a vault. Walt notices whose ears are pink: Robin's. Robin wanted the leak all along; she can't say feelings out loud, so she borrowed the person who does. Lily sings the secret. Mold, the toaster song's sequel, the Stormtrooper was true, and Lily finally keeps one secret: Ted's crush.

beats.line: Guys. I have a confession. And it's true, which is new for me.
I don't know Lily's secret. But the poker face? That's mine. I trained her.
You taught my wife to lie?
She asked nicely. She brought muffins. In hindsight, the muffins were a lie.
Now it's out of control. This morning she told a tourist the Empire State Building is in Ohio.
He went, Ted. He's in Columbus.
So untrain her.
I can't. I lie to strangers so they never really know me. She's lying to the people who know her best.
That's not legendary. That's just lonely.
Did you just have a feeling?
I'll deny it under oath. Which is why I brought backup.
Walt Krupnik. She beat me last Tuesday. I've been in therapy since Wednesday.
Barney. Is this an intervention?
Is it?
Lily, I don't need the secret. I just miss you telling me stuff.
You tell me your dreams. The plots of commercials. When a stranger on the bus has nice hands.
Our whole marriage is you telling me everything, and me saying, no way. I miss saying no way.
Marshmallow. I promised.
Her ears are white as milk, son. She's a vault.
But that one. Left ear's been pink since the door opened.
It's windy. I'm Canadian. Our ears just do that.
Every time somebody says just tell us, it gets pinker. You're not hiding it, ma'am. You're rooting for it.
Lily. Just tell us.
Pinker.
Robin. You wanted me to blab?
Obviously! I gave you the whisper, the threat, the deadline! You blab faster under pressure!
You were supposed to crack by dinner! I practiced a surprised face! And then you went to Barney!
You're welcome.
Why didn't you just tell them yourself?
Because then I'd have to say it out loud. With feelings. And Marshall would hug me.
Robin, I'm going to hug you no matter what it is.
I know. That's the problem.
Lily, you don't blab because you're weak. When something good happens to someone you love, it just doesn't fit inside you.
You love people out loud. I can't. So I borrowed you.
That's the nicest thing anyone's ever said about my worst quality.
So I can tell them?
They're standing right there. Go.
Robin bought an apartment! Thirty-year mortgage! She's staying forever!
I'm knitting you a doormat.
Called it.
I get the keys Friday. You're all coming. Don't make it weird.
Is it pre-war? Tell me there's crown molding.
There's mold.
Wait. A week of training, a polygraph, a man in Columbus, and the big secret was real estate?
Disgusting. I'm so proud. I'm bringing champagne.
Marshmallow, I love Bigfoot, there's no Dr. Pell, and there's a commercial with a sad horse I have to tell you about.
No way!
Oh, and Barney? The Stormtrooper thing was true.
Ted!
It was raining. He looked cold.
Wait. So who has the crush on me?
Vault.
True.
That Friday, Lily told the doorman, both movers and the shelf-liner guy. Barney swore off apprentices forever.
Good. Because Uncle Barney definitely never taught me anything.
Penny. Your left ear just went pink.
